d1-seam-discriminate.title: Deciding question: two-world seam discrimination
d1-seam-discriminate.imperative: Build World H (compliant close, never over the line) and World D (runaway begin then closes the same way) yourself; run current at the seam in each. The rendered output must differ and D must name the true total.
d1-seam-discriminate.finding: Built my own two-world seam probe (probe_two_worlds.py, real CLI subprocess, real gauge stamped from the clock, no mocks). World H (compliant, never over the line, advance --why, stop): seam LIVE=None, HIST=None. World D (refused+released begin at g2, then that SAME agent closes g2 with advance --why): seam LIVE=None (correctly cleared -- keying untouched), HIST='TRIP HISTORY: 2 begin(s)...'. Seam output differs between H and D (True), and D names the true total on disk (2==2, True). B1's exact defect (green-in-both-worlds) does not recur.

d2-silencing.title: Can the historical line be silenced?
d2-silencing.imperative: Attempt every close verb, reopen, block/resume, skip, waive, amend, attach, --dry-run, a why_exempt spine, a spine with no why_trail, to clear TRIP HISTORY while an over-the-line begin is on disk and a gate is still active.
d2-silencing.finding: Built my own silencing-attempts probe (probe_silencing.py) against a real over-hard runaway with an armed begin on disk, targeting 9 attack shapes: (1) reopen the closed runaway gate -- REFUSED by the HARD begin-guard itself (reopen is a TRIP_HARD_GUARDED_VERB), and the refusal ADDS a 3rd ledger entry, so the historical count grows, not shrinks; (2) block+resume -- no effect, HIST unchanged; (3) skip -- succeeds but HIST unchanged; (4) advance --mechanical -- REFUSED by no-silent-close, gate stays in-progress, HIST unchanged; (5) amend retext-check on the gate's imperative -- refused for an unrelated schema reason, and amend ops never touch trip_ledger regardless; (6) attach arbitrary evidence after close -- succeeds, HIST unchanged; (7) --dry-run -- not a recognized CLI flag (usage error); (8) a why_exempt gate with no why_trail ever -- live selector matches (None==None per its own documented behavior) so BOTH lines render, and even --mechanical is refused at/over hard regardless of why_exempt, so nothing closes and HIST is untouched. In all 8 in-scope attempts, trip_ledger is append-only and no legal verb sequence cleared or reduced the historical line while a gate remained active. (9) A 9th case -- closing every remaining gate so there is no active gate at all -- does silence BOTH lines via current, but this is pre-existing _trip_advisory behavior (active_id(cl) is None -> '' immediately), not something the rework introduced, and the underlying trip_ledger data is never deleted -- it remains readable directly. Recorded as a non-blocking observation/triage candidate, not a B1 recurrence, since B1 was specifically about the record vanishing while a next reader (fresh agent or ) is still being advised about an ACTIVE gate.

d3-cannot-fail.title: Mirror defect: can the historical line fail to pass?
d3-cannot-fail.imperative: Confirm the live line still behaves as close criterion (b) intends, and that the historical line reads as a historical fact rather than a permanent, unclearable present-tense verdict that gates any action.
d3-cannot-fail.finding: Mirror-defect check. The live line's behavior is unchanged (confirmed by d1/d4/d11): a genuinely fresh understanding (world H, or the offender's own close per B1) reads the live line as absent, so close criterion (b) still holds. The historical line is worded in present-tense-historical framing ('are on the record across this checklist's full history') distinct from the live line's present-tense-current framing ('are on the record under this understanding'), and it gates NOTHING mechanically -- no verb is refused, no postcondition depends on it, it is pure advisory text on the read-only  path. So while it is true no close can ever clear it (by design, confirmed via d2's silencing attempts), it is not 'a check that cannot pass' in the mechanism sense: nothing an agent does is blocked or judged by its presence. It functions as an immutable audit fact, not a per-understanding compliance gate. This is the intended, documented design (docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md 'The fourth' limit) and not a defect.

triage_candidates.statement: Consolidate begin_over_line_records and begin_over_line_records_historical's near-duplicate filter loop into one shared helper (unkeyed base filter, with the live selector applying its own why_ref filter on top) -- pure simplification, no behavior change, out of scope for the narrow B1 rework.

Once a checklist has no active gate (every gate closed), current's trip advisory (both TRIP LEDGER and TRIP HISTORY) goes silent by design (active_id(cl) is None -> _trip_advisory returns '' immediately) -- pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this rework. The underlying trip_ledger data is never deleted and remains directly readable, but no current CLI verb surfaces trip history once a checklist is DONE. Worth a design decision at Commander/Admiral tier: should closeout (e.g. the archive gate) surface trip_ledger history, or is 'read the JSON directly' the intended audit path?
